main_text.head: ODE MONOCOLOS, IN SVBLATVM MERITA MORTE GVISIVM.

p.i: ANNOSAE Thetidis fluctiuagum pecus, Regnatæque domus Nereidum choro Mirantes validæ pondera dexteræ, Quæ puppes pelago nuper Ibericas Imis prætumidas fluctibus obruit, Stant fixæ, veluti dum stupor irruens Furatur vigilum munera sensuum.
Et sint muta licet monstra natantia, Clamant illa tamen mirificæ manus Fortem non solito more potentiam.
Quotquot terra parens continet incolas, Et qui soliuagis montibus incubant, Camporumque tenent æquora qui procul.
Aer quotquot habet lympidus hospites, Testantes, celebrant eximiam Dei Fortis non solito more potentiam.
Nos qui sydereis fornicibus bonæ Auræ particulam ducimus, & sumus Haud mentis vacui, flammea quam fides Illustrat radiis non morientibus, Robur suspicimus, summe Deus, tuum.

page.notes: No running head, as the page opens the ode. Woodcut ornament at the top and historiated initial A are decorative and not transcribed beyond the letter itself. Reading of "fluctiuagum" (ct ligature) and "Testantes" is slightly uncertain but legible.
